claim_scope: Candidate C9c-11, answering the third external pass, which moved the chain D+ to C+ and said precisely what still stood between it and B. (1) THE PACKET FROZE BEHAVIOUR THAT NO LONGER EXISTED. Both the module and the pinned nonclaim still described the no-witness residue that C9c-10 removed. Safe-direction drift, but a P commit's whole purpose is to freeze an accurate boundary, and this is the same claims-lag-code defect the campaign has now committed in five separate candidates. Corrected in both, and the module says plainly that there is no residue any more. (2) THE LAST DERIVE-THEN-REJECT, at the private boundary: the checker runs FOUR witness passes and this module mirrored three -- REQUIRED, FRAGMENT, HEADER -- but not UNEXPECTED, which runs before them. A witness supplied for a lane that must not carry one was derived against and refused by the checker; all twelve slots reproduced it. PROJECTION_WITNESS_UNEXPECTED, caller_input, tested over every slot. Mirroring three of four passes is the same defect as copying the fragment comparison without the header comparison beside it: the complement of what the guard reads is where the next counterexample lives. (3) THE STANDING GATE WAS ONE-DIRECTIONAL. It caught under-refusal and would have stayed GREEN under the over-broad zero-row rule that was written once in this campaign and reverted -- a refusal of states the checker accepts. A same-key zero pair, which the checker accepts, is now pinned among the DERIVED cases; reintroducing the over-broad rule turns the gate red. A gate that only catches under-refusal teaches its author to over-refuse. Still open and named: two coupled zero-external helper refusals that have exactly one accepted candidate each, which this module declines rather than derives.

nonclaims: This packet establishes no production, settlement, release, migration, proof-receipt, or value-moving authority.
The projection has no consumer: no publisher, verifier, or client calls it, so it refuses nothing at runtime.
The projection verifies no receipt; a binding root it accepts is bound to a receipt only where the caller obtained it from an admission witness, and the projection cannot tell the difference.
Multi-lane field ownership is undecided: more than one enabled lane is refused rather than apportioned.
The projection does not establish that the state is correct, only that a certificate over it reconciles.
The projection has NO Rust twin, against this cycle's convention that a Python authority carries one; the Rust checker therefore has no derived-certificate path and no parity vectors for one.

The certificate's source-principal and terminal controlling-principal bindings CONSTRAIN but do not DETERMINE: each binds to SOME controlled location of the fragment, so a cell controlled by two principals admits two certificates that pass every row, partition and aggregate check over one state, with different allocation roots. NOT two ACCEPTED certificates: under the current registry the full checker refuses both (RECEIPT_WITNESS_REQUIRED), which test_an_undetermined_state_admits_two_row_checked_certificates_with_different_roots asserts. The projection refuses such a state rather than choosing.

Under the current registry ELEVEN of the thirteen row cases are masked by PROJECTION_ROWS_BEYOND_PRODUCER before their own code can fire, and TWO reach their own code through the public entry point (entitlements exceeding custody, and controlled atoms no obligation can absorb) -- which test_which_row_cases_the_entry_point_reaches_is_pinned pins as a partition rather than restating. The ten are exercised through the module helpers and state the contract a future producer would have to meet, not behaviour any registered lane exhibits today.
The fixture partition is a statement about the twenty-nine golden states only. It is not a general property of the projection, and the general form of it was false before this cut.
A projection refusal says this state determines no single acceptable certificate; it does not say the state is invalid, and no consumer acts on either answer.

The projection compares a supplied witness; it does not verify one. Given lane_witnesses -- the same slots the checker requires -- a fragment that differs from the one the witness carries is refused (PROJECTION_WITNESS_FRAGMENT_DRIFT, a caller_input code) rather than derived. WITHOUT them the earlier behaviour stands: a state whose rows differ from the ones the committed lane root's receipt admitted still projects to a certificate, which the checker's witness pass then refuses. Both P41 reviewers asked for this residue in a numbered nonclaim and C9c-5 put it only in claim 2 and the claim_scope (opus2 P42 P3-5).
